children: STOXX DIPS BUT SET FOR FIFTH MONTHLY GAIN

was down about 0.1% in morning trade on Monday as rising crude prices and elevated bond yields sapped risk appetite at the end of another positive month that has pushed the pan-European index to fresh record highs.
The STOXX has gained about 0.8% so far in August and is set for a fifth straight monthly advance, underpinned by resilient earnings and gains in technology and basic resources stocks.
On Monday, weakness was concentrated in the tech, real estate, industrials and healthcare, while energy stocks were boosted by the surge in oil prices.
London was shut for a bank holiday, making for a subdued session. The FTSE 100
has lost about 0.4% in August, snapping a four-month winning streak.
